title: HELP! I'm getting too BIG (Hypertrophy Log #5)
summary: NH narrates a garage-gym arm day built from two giant sets (hangman rope curls, paused dips, band flies, belt-squat-machine rows, then leaning preacher curls, twisting sit-ups, skull crushers, snow angels) and explains how he designs an arm day. He then tours his new basement home gym and its equipment.
claims: Advanced lifters should skew exercises toward weak points; beginners just need overall mass
On pronated curls keep the shoulders stacked; shrugging turns it into an upright row
It took him a long time of mobility work to reach 15-20 bodyweight dips; he now does weighted dips with 90 lb for sets of 5
He did paused dips well short of failure to get chest and triceps work while nursing elbow tendonitis, which is now gone
In a giant set, alternate taxing movements with easier ones; you can't have 3-4 very taxing movements in a row
The belt squat machine row hits the lower lats better than any row he's tried, with no lower-back involvement; 6-10 reps with a pause in the stretch
On single-arm dumbbell preacher curls, leaning forward on each rep (learned from Ovak) gives more biceps stretch while the shoulder follows; novices should avoid it
Don't use the lean-forward preacher technique to lift more weight than you can comfortably rep for 8-12
Train abs with full range and slow tempo, never rebounding, so the abs stretch and catch the weight
An arm day shouldn't be crammed with junk arm volume; it should be a low-stress day that still trains the back, abs and prehab
Train the upper back whenever you can, every day if possible, because it has near-infinite potential
On his upper/lower/arms split: lower back, RDLs and hamstrings on lower days; lats on upper and arm days
Do skull crushers with elbows pointing behind the head for more stretch, pause at the bottom, and dump the dumbbells at the end so you can reach failure
Push isolation work to failure; there's no reason not to
Low-cost prehab like modified snow angels moves the upper back through full range; you can't keep growing if you're injured or in pain
He doesn't believe in a natural limit; even at 6 ft and 215 lb as an advanced lifter he can keep growing
He hasn't deadlifted in 6-7 months and has quit benching, replacing it with dips and push-ups
A belt squat machine (about $1,000) is worth it: he uses it for squats, rows, single-leg RDLs and shrugs, which beat any other shrug
A neck harness is far better than plate neck curls; he regrets not buying one sooner
Wrist cuffs for laterals and triceps extensions mean only the target muscle limits the set
Build your own lifting platform from Home Depot for about $100 rather than paying $1,000 for a Rogue one
Keep a written list of the weight you use for each exercise variation in your home gym
Wrestling shoes are the best general lifting shoes; he uses Olympic weightlifting shoes for squats
exercises: Hangman curl (rope looped around plates or cable, pronated)
shoulders stacked and stationary; cable pulled diagonally for more stretch
biases brachioradialis and brachialis; easy to grind
tie band to rack; go extra deep
stretch and blood flow, easiest at the bottom
strap up; pause in the stretch; 6-10 reps
best lower-lat row, no lower-back limit
lean forward each rep with the shoulder; 8-12 reps
more stretch on biceps; advanced lifters only
full ROM, slow tempo, no rebound
elbows pointed behind head, pause at bottom, dump the dumbbells at failure
